unboxing: Remove protective orange shipping locks from scanner and internal components
Connect power cable to main unit
Power on device using main power switch
initialSetup: Select language and region on touch screen
Set date, time, and time zone
Register device with Canon cloud services (optional)
Print configuration report to verify setup

ethernet: Connect CAT6 Ethernet cable to RJ-45 port on rear
On touch screen: Settings/Registration > Network > TCP/IP Settings
Choose Auto Obtain (DHCP) or configure Static IP
Print Network Status Report to verify
Access Remote UI at https://[printer-ip] (HTTPS recommended)
wifi: Requires optional Canon Wireless LAN Kit
Install wireless kit in designated slot
Power on device and navigate to Network Settings
Choose network SSID and enter WPA2/WPA3 password
Confirm connection and print network status
Note: Ethernet recommended for enterprise deployment

driverInstallation.windows: Download Generic Plus PCL6 driver from Canon website. Run installer and select network search. For enterprise deployment, use Canon's Universal Print Driver for fleet-wide installation.
driverInstallation.mac: Download Canon Mac driver from support website. Install and add printer via System Preferences > Printers & Scanners. Device supports AirPrint for driver-free printing.
driverInstallation.linux: Download Canon Linux UFRII driver. Extract and run installer script. Configure via CUPS interface. PPD files available for most distributions.

configPages.meterPage: Touch screen: Main Menu > Counter > Print Counter List. Shows total impressions, copies, prints, scans, and consumable status.
configPages.configPage: Main Menu > Settings/Registration > Output Reports > Configuration Page. Prints complete device settings including network, security, and feature status.
configPages.networkConfigPage: Main Menu > Settings/Registration > Output Reports > Network Status Report. Shows IP, MAC, DNS, WINS, and all network protocol settings.
configPages.webInterface: Access Remote UI by entering device IP in web browser (https://192.168.1.100). Default admin login required. Configure HTTPS certificate for secure access. Remote UI provides complete device management, user administration, and fleet monitoring capabilities.

commonIssues: After initial setup, configure Scan and Send settings via Remote UI > Device Settings > Send
Set up LDAP integration for enterprise address book: Remote UI > Address Book Management
Configure department ID management for cost tracking if required
Enable audit logging for security compliance: Settings > Security Settings
For uniFLOW integration, install uniFLOW connector and configure authentication
Update firmware via Remote UI > Device Management > Firmware Update (requires Canon support account)

solutions: Power off device completely using main power switch
Wait 30 seconds
Power back on and allow full initialization
Check scanner cable connections
If error persists, contact Canon service - may require technician
Do not attempt to disassemble scanner unit

causes: Fixing unit at end of life
solutions: Power off device for 15 minutes to allow cooling
Power back on
Check fixing unit page count (replace at rated life)
Verify fixing unit is properly seated
Error may require Canon certified technician
Fixing unit replacement is covered under most service contracts
Follow on-screen instructions to locate jam
Open indicated cover and remove all jammed paper
Check paper quality and reload correctly
Ensure paper guides are properly adjusted
Clean feed rollers if jams are recurring
Replace pickup rollers if excessively worn

causes: Cartridge memory chip dirty or damaged
solutions: Remove toner cartridge
Clean cartridge memory contacts with dry lint-free cloth
Verify using genuine Canon GPR-57 toner
Reinstall cartridge ensuring it clicks into place
Close front cover firmly
If error persists, try different genuine Canon cartridge
Update firmware if using new toner batch

accessInstructions: Identify which drawer from touch screen display
Pull drawer completely out of device
Look for jammed paper at rear of drawer cavity
clearanceSteps: Remove all paper from drawer
Check for damaged sheets and discard
Remove any jammed paper from feed area
Check pickup roller condition
Reload paper ensuring stack is below max line
Adjust front and side guides to match paper size exactly
Reinsert drawer completely until it clicks
prevention: Use only paper within 52-300 g/m² specification
Fan paper before loading to prevent static
Do not mix different paper types in same drawer
Store paper in climate-controlled environment (20-25°C, 50-70% RH)
Replace pickup rollers at recommended intervals

accessInstructions: WARNING: Fixing unit is extremely hot - wait 30 minutes after power off
Open right door of main unit
Fixing unit is large assembly at rear
clearanceSteps: WAIT for fixing unit to cool completely
Pull green release lever on fixing unit
Gently remove jammed paper in direction of arrows
Do NOT touch fuser rollers - oils from skin cause print defects
Check for torn pieces and remove all paper fragments
Close right door firmly
Run test print to verify
prevention: Use correct paper weight setting in driver
Avoid printing on damp or curled paper
Replace fixing unit at rated life (300k pages for this model)
Keep fixing unit clean - schedule professional maintenance

accessInstructions: Open rear door (left side of device)
Locate duplex unit - blue lever visible
clearanceSteps: Pull blue lever to release duplex unit
Slide duplex unit out partially
Remove jammed paper carefully
Check duplex path for obstructions or torn pieces
Slide duplex unit back in until it locks
Close rear door
Run duplex test print
prevention: Use 60-120 g/m² paper for duplex printing
Avoid heavily textured or pre-punched paper for duplex
Clean duplex rollers during scheduled maintenance
Ensure paper is completely dry before loading

accessInstructions: Location indicated on touch screen display
clearanceSteps: Follow on-screen prompts for specific finisher jam location
Open indicated finisher cover
Remove jammed sheets
Check stapler unit for misfed staples
Close all finisher covers
Test stapling and finishing functions
prevention: Use only Canon-approved paper for stapling
Do not exceed stapling capacity (typically 50 sheets)
Replace staple cartridge before completely empty

diagnosticSteps: Print Network Status Report from touch screen
Verify IP address is valid and on correct subnet
Check Ethernet cable is securely connected
Test with different Ethernet cable and switch port
Verify network switch port is active and auto-negotiating correctly
solutions: If using DHCP, verify DHCP server has available addresses in pool
Assign static IP if DHCP is problematic
Check firewall rules aren't blocking device
Disable HTTP and enable HTTPS only for security
Update device firmware via USB if network update fails
Reset network settings to defaults: Network > Reset Network Settings
Configure DNS servers manually if auto-config fails
For enterprise networks, verify VLAN configuration matches policy

diagnosticSteps: Access Remote UI and navigate to Send Settings
Test SMTP server connectivity from another device
Review send logs in Remote UI > Log
solutions: Configure SMTP in Remote UI: Device Settings > Send > Email Settings
SMTP Server: smtp.office365.com or smtp.gmail.com
Port: 587 (STARTTLS) or 465 (SSL)
Enable SMTP authentication
Use app-specific password for Office 365/Gmail
Configure correct From address (must be valid email)
Test with internal SMTP server first

diagnosticSteps: Test folder access from Windows PC with same credentials
Review security event logs on file server
solutions: Configure in Remote UI: Address Book > Register Destination
Use IP address instead of hostname: \\192.168.1.10\scans
Enter domain\username and password with Write access to share
Enable SMB2 or higher: Settings > Network > SMB Settings
On Windows server, enable SMB1 temporarily for testing (not recommended long-term)
Verify user has explicit write permissions to destination folder
Disable password-protected sharing on Windows for initial testing
For Active Directory environments, use domain credentials
Check Windows Firewall allows SMB traffic
Test with simple share first (e.g., \\server\test) before complex paths

symptoms: Canon PRINT app can't find device
diagnosticSteps: Verify device and mobile on same network/subnet
Check Bonjour/mDNS is enabled on network
Verify wireless is enabled if using Wi-Fi
solutions: Enable Apple AirPrint: Settings > Network > AirPrint Settings > Use AirPrint: On
Enable Mopria: Settings > Network > Mopria > Enable Mopria
Disable AP isolation on wireless router
Install Canon PRINT Business app (iOS/Android)
For Android: Use Canon Print Service plugin
Enable NFC for tap-and-print (requires optional NFC kit)
Update device firmware for latest mobile printing features
Check mobile device can ping printer IP address

procedure: Open front door of device
Grasp toner cartridge handle and pull straight out
Remove new GPR-57 cartridge from packaging
Rock cartridge gently 5-6 times to distribute toner evenly
Remove protective seal and tape
Insert cartridge until it clicks into place
Close front door - counter resets automatically

generalMaintenance.frequency: Every 80,000 pages or when 'Replace Drum' message appears
procedure: Order C-EXV51 drum unit in advance
Open front door and remove toner cartridge
Release drum unit lock lever (blue)
Pull drum unit straight out
Remove new drum from packaging - do NOT touch drum surface
Remove all protective covers from new drum
Insert new drum until it locks into place
Reinstall toner cartridge
Close front door
Reset drum counter: Main Menu > Adjustment/Maintenance > Reset Counter > Drum

generalMaintenance.frequency: Every 54,000 pages or when 'Replace Waste Toner Container' appears
procedure: Order WT-A3 waste toner container
Open front door
Locate waste toner container (right side, orange)
Pull container straight out - keep level to avoid spillage
Seal old container with cap (included with new container)
Insert new waste toner container until it clicks
Close front door - counter resets automatically
Dispose of old container per local e-waste regulations

generalMaintenance.frequency: Weekly for high-volume environments, monthly otherwise
procedure: Lift scanner unit / Platen cover
Spray glass cleaner on lint-free cloth (not directly on glass)
Wipe scanner glass, document glass, and white reference plate
Clean ADF feed rollers with damp cloth
Allow all surfaces to dry completely
Close scanner unit
Run test scan to verify no streaks

Lubrication of all mechanical assemblies
Firmware update to latest version
Comprehensive diagnostic tests
Calibration and adjustment procedures
Reset all maintenance counters
Typically covered under Canon service contract or can be purchased per-incident

generalMaintenance.task: Clean feed rollers and separation pads
generalMaintenance.frequency: Every 50,000 pages or when frequent jams occur
procedure: Power off device
Open all paper drawers
Locate pickup rollers at rear of each drawer opening
Dampen lint-free cloth with water (no chemicals)
Wipe rollers to remove paper dust and debris
Rotate rollers to clean entire surface
Clean separation pads in drawer
Allow to dry completely (15 minutes)
Reload paper and test feed from each drawer
